messages.content:
You are FOXO's lifestyle coach. Using the doctor's review of a member's lab results, write a practical diet and lifestyle plan for a member living in India.

Rules:
1. Respect the member's diet, allergies and conditions in every item:
   - vegetarian: no meat, fish, seafood or eggs
   - eggetarian: eggs are fine; no meat, fish or seafood
   - vegan: no animal products, including dairy, ghee and honey
   - jain: vegetarian with no eggs, no honey, no onion or garlic, and no root vegetables (potato, carrot, beetroot, radish, ginger and similar)
   - allergies: never include the allergen in any form
   - diabetes: no sugar, jaggery, honey, sweets or sweetened drinks
2. Each diet recommendation must target one of the abnormal biomarkers in the doctor's findings. Put that biomarker's name in linked_biomarker, written as in the findings.
3. Never contradict the doctor's lifestyle_restrictions. If the doctor restricts exercise, suggest only gentle activity such as an easy walk, and tell the member to follow the doctor's advice.
4. Do not recommend medicines or supplements and never give doses. If a supplement might help, say "ask your FOXO doctor".
5. Use everyday Indian foods (dal, millets, seasonal sabzi, sprouts and so on) and be specific about portions and timing.
6. Put foods to eat in diet_recommendations and foods to limit or avoid in foods_to_avoid.
7. retest_in_weeks is usually 12.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"DietRecommendation": {"properties": {"item": {"title": "Item", "type": "string"}, "rationale": {"title": "Rationale", "type": "string"}, "linked_biomarker": {"title": "Linked Biomarker", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["item", "rationale", "linked_biomarker"], "title": "DietRecommendation", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"focus_areas": {"items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Focus Areas", "type": "array"}, "diet_recommendations": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/DietRecommendation"}, "title": "Diet Recommendations", "type": "array"}, "foods_to_avoid": {"default": [], "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Foods To Avoid", "type": "array"}, "activity": {"title": "Activity", "type": "string"}, "sleep": {"title": "Sleep", "type": "string"}, "retest_in_weeks": {"title": "Retest In Weeks", "type": "integer"}}, "required": ["focus_areas", "diet_recommendations", "activity", "sleep", "retest_in_weeks"], "title": "CoachPlan", "type": "object"}

response: {"focus_areas":["Improve HbA1c with fixed meal timings and controlled carbohydrate portions","Lower LDL with soluble fiber and reduced fried/full-fat foods","Keep all meals Jain-friendly: no onion, garlic, root vegetables or honey","Keep all foods peanut-free due to allergy"],"diet_recommendations":[{"item":"At breakfast, eat 2 medium moong dal chillas with 1 cup cooked spinach and 1 small bowl of mint-coriander chutney (no onion/garlic), or 1 small bowl (30 g dry) steel-cut oats cooked in water with 1/2 cup diced apple and no honey or sugar.","rationale":"A protein-and-fiber breakfast with whole grains or dal helps slow blood-sugar rise and supports better HbA1c control.","linked_biomarker":"hba1c"},{"item":"At lunch, use a plate method: 1/2 plate non-root seasonal sabzi and salad (gourd, beans, spinach, cabbage, capsicum, cucumber, tomato), 1/4 plate 1 katori (150 g cooked) toor or moong dal, and 1/4 plate 2 small jowar or bajra rotis or 1 cup cooked millet rice. Avoid onion, garlic and root vegetables.","rationale":"High-fiber dal, millets and non-root vegetables lower the glycemic load of the meal and support HbA1c reduction.","linked_biomarker":"hba1c"},{"item":"At 4–5 pm, eat 30 g roasted chana or 1 small bowl (100 g) moong sprouts chaat with lemon, coriander and cucumber; do not add onion, garlic or peanuts.","rationale":"A measured high-fiber, protein snack reduces hunger and helps avoid sweet or fried evening foods that raise blood sugar.","linked_biomarker":"hba1c"},{"item":"Finish dinner by 7:30–8 pm: 1 cup cooked foxtail or bajra millet khichdi with 1/2 cup moong dal and 1 cup non-root vegetables such as lauki, tinda, beans or palak; or 2 bajra rotis with 1 katori palak dal and 1 katori cabbage sabzi.","rationale":"An early, portion-controlled dinner with millets and dal improves overnight blood-sugar control and supports HbA1c.","linked_biomarker":"hba1c"},{"item":"Include one soluble-fiber food daily: 1 medium guava or apple, 1 cup cooked oats, 1 katori cooked okra (bhindi), or 1 tablespoon ground flaxseed mixed into curd or vegetables.","rationale":"Soluble fiber helps bind cholesterol in the gut and supports LDL reduction; fruit portions are kept small for diabetes.","linked_biomarker":"ldl"},{"item":"For cooking and toppings, keep total oil to about 3 teaspoons per day (mustard, rice bran or olive oil), choose steamed/boiled/grilled foods, and if your doctor agrees, use only 1 small handful (15 g) unsalted almonds or walnuts as a snack.","rationale":"Reducing total fat and replacing fried foods with measured healthy fats helps lower LDL while keeping calories controlled.","linked_biomarker":"ldl"}],"foods_to_avoid":["Sugar, jaggery, honey, sweets, mithai, sweetened drinks, fruit juices and sherbets","Peanuts/groundnuts and any food containing them, including peanut chutney, peanut oil and groundnut sweets","Onion, garlic, and root vegetables such as potato, carrot, beetroot, radish, ginger and similar (Jain diet)","Deep-fried and high-fat foods: puri, samosa, pakora, vada, chips, biscuits, white bread, maida naan and bakery items","Full-fat paneer, butter, ghee and cream in large amounts; use only small measured portions if at all","Meat, fish, seafood and eggs (Jain diet)"],"activity":"Follow your doctor's advice. As no exercise restriction is noted, aim for a 15–20 minute easy walk after meals, building to 30 minutes of brisk walking on most days; add light bodyweight exercise 2 days a week only if your doctor agrees. Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or breathlessness.","sleep":"Aim for 7–8 hours nightly with fixed sleep and wake times; finish dinner by 7:30–8 pm, avoid screens for 1 hour before bed, and avoid heavy late-night meals.","retest_in_weeks":12}
